description:
FILED + FIXED s518e (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-17) from the Type-Tiny census (t/21-types/*.t row "Types::Standard knows it has type X").

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs main 5c5a5679):

    no strict 'refs';
    ${"L::C"} = {a => 1}; my $c1 = ${"L::C"}; print ref($c1), "\n";            # perl HASH, PCL ''
    ${"L::A"} = bless {}, "L"; my $a1 = ${"L::A"}; print ref($a1), "\n";   # perl L, PCL ''
    print ref(${"L::C"}), "\n";                                                # both HASH (no assignment)

CAUSE: p-cast-$'s symbolic arm answered the cell's VALUE.  A reference in a PCL scalar is a ref-shaped value (hash table / array vector / function / box) whose bless lives on the CELL; the consumer reads `${...}` as a VARIABLE, so box-set took a bare hash table for `%h` in scalar context (its count) and the class was lost.  The static read `$L::C` passes the cell itself.

=== DONE (s518e) ===
cl/pcl-runtime.lisp p-cast-$: a ref-shaped value answers the CELL (%p-symref-box), as the static read does; a plain value is unchanged.  Guard Pl/t/symref-package-01.t row 19 (perl oracle: blessed / hash / array / code / scalar refs, a plain value, the META ||= idiom, a copy that does not alias), fails on main.  Related, NOT fixed: #3390 (the element-held ref-to-ref read, the write-side sibling).
subject: `my $v = ${"Pkg::name"}` when the package scalar holds a REFERENCE is not a reference: a hash/array ref arrives as its COUNT, a blessed one loses its class -- silent wrong; Type::Library's `${"$class\::META"} ||= bless {}, $class` answers '' on every call after the first (has_type, type_names)
